transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-07-09 14:00 PDT
- Duration: 52 min
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Laura Kim (Head of ML), Omar Reyes (CTO), Priya Singh (Lead DE), Nina Alvarez (PM)

Summary: quick scoping for a 4-week POC to validate open-model options for multilingual clinical summarization and extraction. Primary constraints: PHI-safe handling, low hallucination, throughput for batch ingest of notes, and tight latency for UI (sub-700ms preferred on median).

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, model shortlist tradeoffs, benchmark plan, timeline and infra needs, security requirements, next steps.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): ok hi everyone, thanks for taking the time, um this is Maya from Redwood Inference, with Ethan our solutions engineer
00:07 Dr. Laura Kim: hey hi thanks. quick note, we might have connection hiccups—i'm dialing from the hospital network
00:12 Ethan (Redwood SE): no problem, we'll try to keep slides light and then move to Q&A
00:20 Maya: the goal today is to scope a 3-4 week POC to evaluate a short list of open models for clinical summarization + entity extraction across en/es/pt. we want to confirm perf, cost, and hallucination behavior on your real notes
00:35 Omar (CTO): high level yes. timeline wise we want something we can ship into a pilot in q4; POC needs to show measurable improvement vs our current rule-based summarizer on accuracy and reduced manual edits
00:46 Maya: great, can we confirm success criteria so we put them in the deck — what are the top-line metrics?
00:52 Dr. Laura Kim: primary is QA accuracy on structured extraction for meds/diagnoses (F1 target ~0.88), secondary is summarization fidelity — we use an edit-distance proxy today, target reduce human edits by 40%. latency target is median <700ms for single-note query, and throughput of about 200 RPS for batch ingest windows.
01:12 Priya Singh: to add, we have daily batch jobs that peak at roughly 150k notes/day, average note length ~1,200 tokens; expect spikes up to 250k on some weekdays. storage and data residency: notes must not leave our VPC during pilot unless explicitly anonymized.
01:33 Ethan: ok useful. two infra options for POC: 1) hosted Redwood baseline where we run isolated buckets and token-level audit logs, 2) private dedicated or VPC deployment in your cloud. For initial benchmarking we typically do hosted to get fast numbers then move to private if data residency is required
01:52 Nina Alvarez: we'd prefer private VPC if possible; legal will push back on hosted unless we can show strong anonymization and SOC2 doc.
02:01 Maya: understood — we'll send SOC2 and SSO docs. For the model shortlist — we proposed MPT-30B, Falcon-40B, and Llama-family (3? or 2?). Ethan, can you summarize tradeoffs?
02:15 Ethan: sure. MPT-30B we find is cost-efficient and good for instruction style tasks; Falcon-40B tends to be strong on few-shot summarization but larger memory profile; Llama-3 (open variants) show fidelity on biomedical phrasing but sometimes need more careful system prompts, also quantization behavior differs across stacks. note: some names in notes might be garbled by the speech-2-text, we saw "Lama 3" in earlier docs which is just mis-transcribe
02:45 Omar: curious about hallucination rates — do you have baseline numbers?
02:49 Ethan: rough hosted baselines we've seen: falcon family had hallucination ~8-12% on out-of-domain clinical terms without grounding, llama variants 6-10% when fine-tuned or with retrieval; MPT around 10-14% unless augmented with retrieval. big caveat: numbers vary a lot with prompt set and temperature/decoding settings
03:14 Dr. Laura Kim: we will prioritize hallucination and extraction precision over minor latency differences. Can you plug in retrieval/cache options? We want the model to consult an index of patient-safe canonical terms to reduce hallucination
03:26 Ethan: yes — Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV cache and retrieval hooks; we can wire a vector DB retrieval step in the pipeline. note sometimes the transcripts show K V cash instead of KV cache so apologies if earlier docs were noisy
03:40 Priya: ok good. about multilingual — our Spanish and Portuguese notes are about 25% of volume; we need comparable F1 in those languages. do you have multilingual variants or will we rely on en-models doing well?
03:53 Ethan: two approaches: pick multilingual-capable open models (e.g., some Llama variants fine-tuned for multi), or run language-specific models. running separate models increases infra complexity and cost. for POC we recommend a single multilingual model variant and then evaluate gaps, unless you have strict language parity requirements
04:14 Nina: language parity is desired but not strict for release — we need to see quantitative gaps in POC
04:20 Maya: let's talk about workloads and sizing for benchmarks — Priya mentioned 150k notes/day, 1,200 tokens avg. what's your concurrency shape?
04:31 Priya: batch windows are 4 hours in early morning for the bulk, we prefer to do bulk inference there. interactive UI calls are ~200 RPS but with median note size shorter (400 tokens)
04:44 Ethan: good. from that we plan two benchmark scenarios: 1) batch throughput test: sustained token throughput to show cost/tok and latency tail for large batches; 2) interactive median latency test at 200 RPS and 400 token median. we'll measure median/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. we'll also capture memory/KV cache hit rates for warm runs
05:05 Maya: any constraints on quantization? are you ok with int8/4-bit models?
05:10 Omar: legal will ask — if we do private VPC, quantization is fine. Hosted baseline should use quantized models to be cost-representative but we need to note that quantization sometimes affects hallucination/accuracy
05:23 Ethan: yep will note. we'll run the same prompt sets across fp16 and 4-bit quant settings to compare tradeoffs.
05:30 Dr. Laura Kim: what about evaluation metrics for summarization — are you set on ROUGE or do you recommend human raters for clinical fidelity?
05:38 Ethan: we suggest hybrid: automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, BERTScore) for quick iteration + a small human eval panel (internal clinicians) to score hallucination and clinical safety. for extraction tasks use precision/recall/F1 against annotated gold set
05:52 Maya: good. on security — we will provide SAML SSO for console access, and customer-managed KMS for the private plan. also audit logs at token level are available on Redwood Dedicated — i'll include that in the docs pack
06:08 Priya: can the logs be filtered or redacted? PHI must be redacted at rest
06:13 Ethan: audit logs can be configured to not store raw text for hosted, or to store only hashed ids. for private deployment you can keep everything local to your KMS and HSM if required
06:25 Omar: cost? rough cost numbers for the two-week benchmark or monthly projection at 150k/day?
06:31 Maya: rough ballpark now: hosted baseline for MPT-30B quantized might be $X per 1M tokens, Falcon-40B more expensive due to larger mem and GPU type. we'll share a detailed pricing sheet but for planning assume 30-50% difference between MPT and Falcon in hosted unit cost
06:50 Dr. Laura Kim: ok fine. can we define the POC acceptance criteria now?
06:55 Maya: propose: 1) extraction F1 >= 0.86 and at least 30% reduction in manual edits on summaries, 2) median interactive latency <700ms, p95 <2.5s, 3) hallucination rate <10% in human eval, and 4) infra plan approved by Sentinel infra/legal for one of the Redwood deployment options
07:20 Nina: that seems reasonable; legal will want to review the SOC2 and KMS flow before sign-off
07:27 Maya: agreed. timeline suggestion: week 0 (this week) collect data + sign NDA and open a cluster, week 1 hosted baseline runs + initial metrics, week 2 focused tuning (prompts/retrieval), week 3 expanded eval including multi-lang and human review, week 4 handoff and recommendation meeting. total ~4 weeks
07:48 Omar: can you compress it to 3 weeks if needed? we prefer 4 but we might compress if the hosted runs are fast
07:55 Ethan: it's possible but we risk under-sampling language or tuning steps; pref 4 weeks for robust signal
08:05 Priya: data handoff — what's the preferred format for the sample?
08:09 Ethan: CSV with id, language tag, raw_text, annotations (for gold extraction), de-id where possible. Priya: ok we'll do 5k records to start
08:20 Maya: sharing links now — will follow up after the call with a drive link to the benchmark sheet and a short deck. link placeholder: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/benchmark-sentinel
08:31 Dr. Laura Kim: perfect. any red flags on private infra?
08:36 Ethan: only things to note: we'll need a small NAT/egress rule set for the console if you use private control plane, and we'll coordinate key exchange for KMS. also network throughput numbers for batch windows (we'll send required bandwidth estimates)
08:52 Maya: ok wrapping up — quick recap of next steps: maya send security + pricing, ethan run hosted baselines and share perf/cost numbers, priya provide data sample, and we schedule infra deep-dive for next week.
09:05 Omar: thanks all.
09:08 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive.
09:12 — End of recording

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (Llama->Lama) and tech terms (KV cache). Some cross-talk when Laura and Omar were on a noisy network. Shared artifacts: "Benchmark spreadsheet (sent by Maya)" https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/benchmark-sentinel and "Redwood SOC2 + security pack" (to be attached).

POC acceptance criteria (re-stated):
- Extraction F1 target >= 0.86 on gold set
- 30% reduction in manual edits for summarization
- Median latency <700ms (interactive) and p95 <2.5s
- Hallucination <10% by clinician human eval

Potential risks called out:
- Multilingual parity may require separate fine-tuning or language-specific models which raises cost
- Quantization impacts on hallucination/accuracy need empirical testing
- Legal/data residency may force private deployment which adds lead time

End transcript.
